newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Strong gasoline demand seen in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Strong gasoline demand seen in APIs.

text.p: REUTER POLL FORECAST* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
UTILIZATION..... UP 0.50 PCT PT 95.0 DN 2.10 PCT PT
*NB - The forecast is derived by polling at least six market analysts, omitting the high and low forecast from and averaging the rest.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected by dealers to report a gasoline inventory decline for the eighth consecutive week as a strong U.S. economy has given Americans a penchant for spending at the pump.

"Gasoline demand continues to run ahead of last year and it is being extended longer into the summer. The strong economy is behind it more than anything else," said Bill O'Grady, energy analyst with A.G. Edwards in St. Louis.
Dealers expect the data will show gasoline stocks fell one to three million barrels. The data reflects the week ended August 14 and is expected to be released Tuesday evening.
Implied gasoline demand had declined to 8.3 million barrels per day (bpd) the week before last from 8.4 million bpd, but the three week average remained at a hefty 8.5 million bpd.

Some refinery problems were expected to have helped rein in gasoline output. Exxon's Baytown refinery in Texas, by most traders estimation, has kept its 110,000 bpd catalytic cracker down after shutting it due to operational problems last week.
Tosco wasn't expected to have restarted its 150,000 bpd cat cracker until this week after shutting it for several weeks due to a leak.

"These refineries as whole are still running, and they are very large, so I think crude may draw one to two million," said O'Grady. Analysts and dealers were actually split about whether crude stocks will decline or increase.

"I think there will be a draw of between 2.5 to 4.5 million (barrels) since we should have a correction to the rise in crude imports last week," said Thomas Blakeslee, trader and analyst with Cargill Investor Services Inc in New York.
Crude imports swelled to 8.6 million bpd in last week's data. Others said refinery problems decreased crude demand and would cause a crude stock build of up to two million barrels.

Still, the refinery utilization rate was expected to rise by a 0.5 percentage point after declining by two percentage points a week earlier. But, the refinery rate was still seen in a general downtrend after holding above 95 percent for much of the summer.

Distillate stocks, composed of diesel and heating oil, were expected to rise up to 2.5 million barrels - a seasonal build given low heating oil demand during summer. However, dealers said the strike by UPS workers may push up distillate stocks even more since the 15-day walk out decreased diesel demand by delivery trucks.
